title: Penn World Table 10.01: the countries with data for 1960 and 2019 and an investment share in every year 1960-2019
series: countrycode and country as in the workbook; in the words of its sheet Legend: rgdpe_1960 ('Expenditure-side real GDP at chained PPPs (in mil. 2017US$)'), rgdpna_1960 and rgdpna_2019 ('Real GDP at constant 2017 national prices (in mil. 2017US$)'), pop_1960 and pop_2019 ('Population (in millions)'), csh_i_mean_1960_2019 (the mean over the 60 years 1960-2019 of csh_i, 'Share of gross capital formation at current PPPs'), hc_1960 ('Human capital index, based on years of schooling and returns to education'; empty where the workbook has none); and the workbook's own flags: csh_i_1960 and csh_i_1961 (csh_i in those years), i_outlier_years (the years 1960-2019 whose i_outlier is 'Outlier', joined with ';'; sheet Legend: 'the observation on pl_gdpe or pl_gdpo is not an outlier (0) or an outlier (1)'), i_xr_1960 and i_xr_2019 (sheet Legend: 'the exchange rate is market-based (0) or estimated (1)')
notes: Read from the workbook pwt1001.xlsx, sheet Data, downloaded from https://dataverse.nl/api/access/datafile/354095 (SHA-256 bf2b66c5fd8b465870eeab8bbfa3a57e73253a3236a933286259efbbb5fb67a2), whose SHA-1, 7461933f7561767ffbd77db3ab984d60cb21e9ef, is the one the dataset record gives. The figures are written as the workbook stores them (Python's repr of the float). The workbook's sheet Info says: 'When using these data, please refer to the following paper:' and gives the same reference. A country is kept when the workbook has rgdpe, rgdpna and pop for 1960 and rgdpna and pop for 2019, and csh_i in every year from 1960 to 2019. checks/check_ch40.py computes from these rows the growth of real GDP per head 1960-2019 (rgdpna/pop, log difference over 59 years), the log of real GDP per head in 1960 (rgdpe/pop), the log of the mean investment share and the log of the growth of population plus 0.05, and the regressions of Table tab:solow-convergence.
source: Penn World Table version 10.01, Groningen Growth and Development Centre, University of Groningen (DataverseNL, doi:10.34894/QT5BCC, released 2023-01-26)
